chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Abu Ubayda, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Is prayer in the entire Haram (Sacred Precinct) the same?' He said, 'O Abu Ubayda! Is prayer in the Sacred Mosque (Masjid al-Haram) all the same? So how can it be the same in the entire Haram?' I said, 'So which part of it is most superior?' He said, 'That which is between the Door and the Black Stone.'

key_terms.الْحَرَمِ: The Sacred Precinct (Haram), referring to the broader sacred area of Mecca.
key_terms.الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ: The Sacred Mosque (Masjid al-Haram), the specific structure containing the Kaaba.

ai.seo_question: Where is the most superior place for prayer within the Haram according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the distinction between the general precincts of Mecca (al-Haram) and the specific sanctuary of the Kaaba (Masjid al-Haram), correcting Abu Ubayda’s conflation of the two. The Imam identifies the most superior spot for prayer as the area between the Door of the Kaaba and the Black Stone, a location historically associated with the Prophet Ibrahim’s construction and the focal point of circumambulation. This narration underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on specific spatial hierarchies within the Sacred Mosque, where proximity to the Kaaba’s structure amplifies the spiritual merit of worship.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Abu Ayoub Al Khazzaz, from Abu Ubeyda who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘The Salaat in the Harram, all of it is the same?’ So heasws said: ‘O Abu Ubeyda! The Salaat in the Sacred Masjid is not the same, and how can it happen to be the same in the Harram?’ I said, ‘So which spot is the most superior?’ Heasws said: ‘What is between the Door (of the Kabah) to the Black Stone’.
en.sarwar: 2. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz from abu ‘Ubaydah who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, if performing Salat (prayer) in all of al-Haram (the sacred area) is of the same degree of virtue. He (the Imam) said, ‘O abu ‘Ubaydah, all Salat (prayer) in Masjid al-Haram are not of the same degree of virtue; then how can it be the same in all of al-Haram (the sacred area)?’ I then asked, ‘Which part of it is more excellent?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is between the door and the Black Stone.’”
